aria: Animated recap of the Bulls' 122 to 108 home win over the Cavaliers: Josh Giddey's finger-roll layup with 7:37 left that made it 113 to 97 and capped a 10 to 0 run, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Tre Jones' 16 points and 9 assists, the top scorers, how the Bulls won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from the Bulls' 122–108 home win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov 23, 2026: the Bulls' player lines are from the CBS Sports box score and the Cavaliers' from the Yahoo Sports box score; all 122 Chicago points and all 108 Cleveland points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (44 of 96, 20 of 49 from three, 14 of 17 FT for Chicago; 36 of 78, 8 of 31, 28 of 32 for Cleveland), assists (35–21), steals (12–4) and turnovers (Cleveland 18). Quarter scores (Cavaliers 30–20–39–19, Bulls 27–45–21–29) from the Yahoo and CBS box scores; 72–50 at the half and 93–89 after three are also in the AP. Bulls lines used here also match written accounts: Hawkins 19, a season high, 7 of 13 with 4 threes (AP; cleveland.com; On Tap Sports Net), Hield 17 with 12 in the fourth (On Tap Sports Net; cleveland.com), Jones 16 with 9 assists and 2 steals (On Tap Sports Net; ClutchPoints), Buzelis 15, all in the first half (AP; ClutchPoints), Okoro 12 and Smith 11 (Yardbarker), Giddey 4 with 11 assists on 2 of 11 (AP); Cleveland's Mitchell 28, Harden 21, Allen 16 and Merrill 12 also match cleveland.com. 20 of 49 from three, 45.8% shooting and 63 bench points are also in the AP. Chicago's 24-point lead at 72–48 is in the AP and the FOX Sports play-by-play; Cleveland's 6-point lead (28–22 in the first quarter) is from the FOX Sports play-by-play.

The Bulls have won two straight (On Tap Sports Net; ClutchPoints; Basketball Network), had 48 bench points in the first half (ClutchPoints; SB Nation), and Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis sat the final 4:41 (On Tap Sports Net; ClutchPoints). Cleveland played without Evan Mobley (sprained toe, cleveland.com); Mitchell played through an illness (cleveland.com). Next: the Bulls visit Charlotte on Wednesday (AP; ClutchPoints); the Cavaliers visit the Knicks on Wednesday (cleveland.com). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Monday's games.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Josh Giddey's finger-roll layup that made it 113–97: AP: "a 10-0 spurt capped by Josh Giddey's finger-roll layup 4:23 in that made it 113-97"; On Tap Sports Net says Giddey blocked Sam Merrill at the rim and then scored in transition to finish the 10–0 run. "4:23 in" is 4:23 into the fourth, so 7:37 left: the CBS Sports play-by-play has Giddey's layups at 8:44 and 7:37 of the fourth, and On Tap has the Bulls at 108–97 with 8:44 left and 113–104 with 4:41 left. The board's Bulls +14 to +16 is 111–97 to 113–97, which follows from the two-point layup. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Chicago Bulls or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Giddey's listed 6-foot-7 and 214 pounds (RealGM), with arms at the default length because no wingspan is reported there, in the Bulls' home kit with No. 3 (RealGM) and the default darker skin tone, since he has no approved look yet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
